educationalGoal: The basis of human behavior is information processing. This course focuses on sense perception (the mental process of sensory input) and cognition (the mental process of information processing). The neural basis and neural disorder of sense perception and cognition will also be introduced. In addition, the opportunity to think about how to apply sensory and perceptual knowledge to information design will be provided.

              1.Sensation
2.Perception
3.Attention
4.Disorder

              The basis of human behavior is information processing. This course focuses on sense perception (the mental process of sensory input) and cognition (the mental process of information processing). The neural basis and neural disorder of sense perception and cognition will also be introduced. In addition, the opportunity to think about how to apply sensory and perceptual knowledge to information design will be provided.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              Lectures will primarily be delivered using slides.
Textbooks of Introduction to Psychology A and B will be used as reference books. Supplementary materials will be distributed for units and charts not included in the reference books.
In addition to lectures, demonstrations and exercises designed to aid understanding of the course content will be incorporated into the lessons.
Please note that the weekly learning content and schedule may be adjusted depending on the progress of the course.
This subject is eligible for the course credit system.

              教科書および参考書・リザーブドブック

              Textbook: None
Reference book: Katori, H., Sugimoto, T., Torii, S., & Kawachi, J. (Eds.) (2020). Psychology, 5th revised ed. University of Tokyo Press (ISBN: 978-4-13-012117-0)

              履修に必要な予備知識や技能

              It is advisable to review what you have learned in Chapter 5 of Introduction to Psychology A. If you find anything in the class content difficult, please refer to reference books or books in the Library Center collection, or ask questions directly to the faculty member. Students are expected to approach class with a positive attitude, deepening their understanding of the knowledge they have learned in class by experiencing it through their own senses and perceptions.
